entities.blurb: The badlands or mesa are an arid-land mountainous biome, featuring red sand and mounds of terracotta bands, coming in various colors. Badlands generate in arid lands next to deserts and their eroded and wooded variants.
entities.name: Badlands

entities.blurb: The basalt deltas are a volcanic biome found in the Nether.
entities.name: Basalt Deltas

entities.blurb: Beaches are common coastal biomes that serve as transition biomes from the mainland to an ocean. Beaches are covered entirely with sand and are the main source of turtles and buried treasure.
entities.name: Beach

entities.blurb: A birch forest is a lush biome filled with birch trees and wildflowers that usually generates near other woodland biomes.
entities.name: Birch Forest

entities.blurb: A cherry grove is a mountain slope and plateau biome similar to meadows, filled with cherry trees.
entities.name: Cherry Grove

entities.blurb: The cold ocean is a cold variant of the ocean biome with slightly less underwater vegetation. It generates near cold biomes and has a deep variant.
entities.name: Cold Ocean

entities.blurb: The crimson forest is a forested biome in the Nether. It is one of two Nether biomes where players are able to acquire wood without returning to the Overworld. This forest is the only place where huge crimson fungus trees grow naturally.
entities.name: Crimson Forest

entities.blurb: A dark forest or roofed forest is a forested biome with dense leaf canopies that block sunlight, allowing hostile mobs to spawn and hide from the sun during daytime. Dark forests are one of the two biomes that woodland mansions can generate in.
entities.name: Dark Forest

entities.blurb: The deep cold ocean is a deep variant of the cold ocean.
entities.name: Deep Cold Ocean

entities.blurb: The deep dark is a cave biome that generates deep underground in the Overworld under mountainous areas. Covered in sculk, no hostile mobs spawn here except for the warden which appears after activating sculk shriekers.
entities.name: Deep Dark

entities.blurb: The deep frozen ocean is a deep variant of the frozen ocean. Unlike the regular frozen ocean, the water surface is not covered with ice, though icebergs still generate in the water.
entities.name: Deep Frozen Ocean

entities.blurb: The deep lukewarm ocean is a deep variant of the lukewarm ocean.
entities.name: Deep Lukewarm Ocean

entities.blurb: A deep ocean is a variant of the regular ocean with the seafloor twice as deep.
entities.name: Deep Ocean

entities.blurb: A desert is an expansive arid biome mainly consisting of sand. It is notable for its many structures such as desert pyramids and villages, and its dangerous hostile mob variants.
entities.name: Desert

entities.blurb: The dripstone caves is a cave biome found in inland areas, filled with clusters and pillars of pointed dripstone and dripstone blocks.
entities.name: Dripstone Caves

entities.blurb: The eroded badlands or mesa bryce biome is a variant of the badlands notable for its hoodoos.
entities.name: Eroded Badlands

entities.blurb: A flower forest is a variant of the forest filled with a much larger variation and frequency of flowers. Rabbits spawn here instead of wolves and bee nests generate much more often.
entities.name: Flower Forest

entities.blurb: The forest is a lush biome densely wooded with oak and birch trees. Woods wolves spawn here. The forest is the most common surface biome in Minecraft, making up about 12% of the Overworld's area.
entities.name: Forest

entities.blurb: The frozen ocean is an icy variant of ocean covered by icebergs. The water's surface is partially covered with ice, where snowfall may occur and polar bears can spawn.
entities.name: Frozen Ocean

entities.blurb: Frozen peaks are snowy mountain peak biomes made out of ice and packed ice and covered by snow blocks.
entities.name: Frozen Peaks

entities.blurb: A frozen river is an ice topped variant of the river that replaces the river in cold regions.
entities.name: Frozen River

entities.blurb: A grove is a snowy forest biome that often generates on the sides of mountains. Similar to the snowy taiga, it is filled with spruce trees but the ground is covered with snow blocks and occasional powder snow patches.
entities.name: Grove

entities.blurb: The ice spikes or ice plains spikes biome is a variant of the snowy plains, featuring ice spikes made of packed ice and other special features.
entities.name: Ice spikes

entities.blurb: The jagged peaks are one of the tall mountain peak biomes. These tall and jagged mountains are completely made out of stone covered by a layer of snow blocks.
entities.name: Jagged Peaks

entities.blurb: The jungle is a lush biome with dense vegetation of jungle trees, oak trees, bamboo, and various smaller plants. Jungles generate in humid and warm areas, often next to forests, and their sparse and bamboo variants.
entities.name: Jungle

entities.blurb: The lukewarm ocean is a lukewarm variant of oceans, notable for its sand floor and warm fish.
entities.name: Lukewarm Ocean

entities.blurb: The lush caves is a temperate cave biome with unique fauna and flora found underground below humid biomes, indicated above ground by azalea trees. Aquatic mobs such as glow squid and tropical fish can spawn here. It is also the only biome where axolotls spawn.
entities.name: Lush Caves

entities.blurb: The mangrove swamp is a wetland biome populated with mud and mangroves where slimes, frogs, and bogged can spawn.
entities.name: Mangrove Swamp

entities.blurb: The meadow is an elevated grassy mountain slope and plateau biome filled with patches of flowers, turquoise-green grass and tall grass, where sheep, donkeys, and rabbits spawn.
entities.name: Meadow

entities.blurb: Mushroom fields or mushroom islands are rare biomes which always generate as islands surrounded by deep oceans. They are the only place in the game where mycelium and mooshrooms are found, and have the special property that no hostile mobs normally spawn in them.
entities.name: Mushroom Fields

entities.blurb: The Nether wastes or hell‌[Bedrock Edition  only] is the most common biome found in the Nether.
entities.name: Nether Wastes

entities.blurb: The ocean is an aquatic biome consisting of water. They are deep bodies of water with the surface at an altitude of Y=63, which is counted as the “sea level” of the world.
entities.name: Ocean

entities.blurb: An old growth birch forest or birch forest mutated is a variant of the birch forest, notable for its trees, which are taller than those found in the normal birch forest.
entities.name: Old Growth Birch Forest

entities.blurb: The old growth pine taiga or mega taiga is a forested biome filled with large 2×2 spruce trees, with the tall trees being mostly arrow-shaped: a thick trunk with few leaves at the top. The ground is made of podzol and coarse dirt and covered by mossy cobblestone rocks.
entities.name: Old Growth Pine Taiga

entities.blurb: The old growth spruce taiga or redwood taiga mutated is a forested biome covered with tall 2×2 spruce trees that grow leaves all around the trunk. The ground is made of podzol and coarse dirt and covered by mossy cobblestone rocks.
entities.name: Old Growth Spruce Taiga

entities.blurb: A pale garden is a rare variant of the dark forest biome with pale oaks and many pale vegetation blocks. Creaking hearts that spawn creakings at night can often be found here.
entities.name: Pale Garden

entities.blurb: The plains are common grassland biomes in the Overworld with wide, open terrain and many flowers.
entities.name: Plains

entities.blurb: A river is a common aquatic biome that cuts through most land biomes. Rivers can serve as borders between various other biomes, and usually lead to oceans, although they are also able to form loops.
entities.name: River

entities.blurb: The savanna is an arid grassland biome, featuring scattered acacia and oak trees. It is populated by warm animal variants, llamas, and armadillos, and villages made of acacia wood are commonly found here.
entities.name: Savanna

entities.blurb: A savanna plateau is a variant of the savanna biome that replaces it at higher elevations and near mountains. The biome features spotted wolves unlike the regular savanna, and lacks villages and pillager outposts.
entities.name: Savanna Plateau

entities.blurb: A snowy beach or cold beach is a snowy variant of the beach biome that replaces it in frozen regions.
entities.name: Snowy Beach

entities.blurb: The snowy plains or ice plains are snow-covered grassland biomes in the Overworld that usually generate near other snowy biomes.
entities.name: Snowy plains

entities.blurb: Snowy slopes are snowy biomes that often generate on the sides of mountains. Unlike the snowy plains, this biome is made out of stone covered with one or more layers of snow blocks and occasional powder snow patches.
entities.name: Snowy Slopes

entities.blurb: A snowy taiga or cold taiga is an icy biome that comprises a snow-covered forest of pine and spruce trees, ferns and large ferns, and sweet berry bushes, usually generating adjacent to or within snowy plains.
entities.name: Snowy Taiga

entities.blurb: A soul sand valley is a dry biome located in the Nether. It is formed of large caverns with Nether fossils and different blocks, mainly including soul sand and soul soil.
entities.name: Soul Sand Valley

entities.blurb: The sparse jungle or jungle edge biome is a sparser variant of the jungle, resembling a lush plains biome with small jungle trees.
entities.name: Sparse Jungle

entities.blurb: Stony peaks are warmer mountain peak biomes completely made out of stone and calcite strips.
entities.name: Stony Peaks

entities.blurb: Sulfur caves are cave biomes composed of sulfur and cinnabar blocks, where sulfur cubes and cave spiders naturally spawn. Sulfur pools with potent sulfur generate here, as well as sulfur spikes.
entities.name: Sulfur Caves

entities.blurb: A swamp or swampland is a wetland biome where slimes, frogs, and bogged can spawn, and it is the only biome where swamp huts can generate. It is vegetated by unique swamp oaks covered in vines, firefly bushes, lily pads, and more.
entities.name: Swamp

entities.blurb: The taiga is a humid and cold biome comprising a grassland forested with small and large ferns, pale aquamarine-green grass, spruce and pine trees. Foxes and wolves commonly spawn here.
entities.name: Taiga

entities.blurb: The End is a biome used to generate the End dimension. There are five biomes in the End, but they are considered separate biomes only in Java Edition, while generating the same terrain as in Bedrock Edition.
entities.name: The End

entities.blurb: The Void is an empty biome which generates the void start platform. It is used by "The Void" superflat preset in Java Edition, and can be set in a single biome world as well. The void biome only exists in Java Edition; in Bedrock Edition, the "The Void" flat world preset is set to the plains biome, but generates identically as in Java Edition.
entities.name: The Void

entities.blurb: The warm ocean is a warm ocean variant filled with coral reefs on a sand-covered floor. Tropical fish and pufferfish spawn here, and sea pickles can generate on the ocean floor.
entities.name: Warm Ocean

entities.blurb: The warped forest is an uncommon forested biome found in the Nether. Endermen are common in this biome, and hostile mobs do not spawn naturally. It is one of two Nether biomes where players are able to acquire wood without returning to the Overworld. The warped forest is the only place where huge warped fungus trees grow naturally.
entities.name: Warped Forest

entities.blurb: The windswept forest or extreme hills plus trees biome is a more humid variant of the windswept hills filled with spruce and oak trees.
entities.name: Windswept Forest

entities.blurb: The windswept gravelly hills or extreme hills mutated biome is a more desolate variant of the windswept hills covered with gravel. It is a relatively rare biome in the Overworld.
entities.name: Windswept Gravelly Hills

entities.blurb: Windswept hills or extreme hills are cold mountainous biomes with shattered terrain covered by grass blocks and stone. Windswept hills generate in areas with high erosion close to swamps, often bordering their wooded and gravelly variants.
entities.name: Windswept Hills

entities.blurb: The windswept savanna or savanna mutated is a shattered and mountainous variant of the savanna that generates in areas with high erosion close to swamps and other windswept biomes. The terrain consists of huge cliffs and floating islands covered with coarse dirt, stone, and savanna vegetation.
entities.name: Windswept Savanna

entities.blurb: The wooded badlands or mesa plateau stone biome is a more humid variant of the badlands covered by grass blocks and coarse dirt on their plateaus, vegetated by small oak trees.
entities.name: Wooded Badlands
